title: MemeSense: An Adaptive In-Context Framework for Social Commonsense Driven Meme Moderation
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the model's ability to detect 'Religious sensitivity' as a type of harmful content. This is defined as content that disrespects religious beliefs, symbols, or historical context, and the task was to generate a textual intervention explaining why such a meme is inappropriate for posting.
findings: The MemeSense framework demonstrated robust performance in generating interventions for memes categorized under 'Empathy and ethical judgements,' which includes the specific parameter 'Religious sensitivity'. The model's performance on this meta-category was high and consistent with its performance on other categories (BERTScore: 0.90, Semantic Similarity: 0.75, ROUGE-L: 0.33), indicating its effectiveness in handling religiously insensitive content.
